items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: So Mingus said, “Okay we’re playing Birdland the next five days” or something like that, opposite the Coltrane quartet.

ctx.x: No, no. So, because I didn’t understand Mingus’ question, I said, “What tunes do you want to hear?” The audience went, “Woooooh.” A challenge being hurled. “Oh you’re bad. Are you bad enough for that? Come on up here and we’re going to see about this.” So that’s what I did. I went and played some blues tune or other. And the audience was cheering. And he said, “On that blues you were doubled up pretty fast on a couple of choruses. You couldn’t play an uptempo tune, could you?” I said, “Yeah, I’m sure I can.” So…

he said, “Okay, you’ve still got the gig but learn how to play ‘Stormy Weather’ right.” So I went, “Well what was wrong with it?” He said, “You know the part that says, ‘It’s raining all the time/it’s raining all the time.’ You have to say that two times.”
